body:
~~[mini.operators] Support visual selection for exhange operator [gx]~~

Is it possible for the `mini.operators` exchange [gx] to support visual selection via `dot-repeat`?

Keys | Description
-- | --
`v`, `gx`, ..., `.` | Exchange a charwise visual selection with an unselected region [1]
`v`, `gx`, ..., `v`, `.` | Exchange a charwise visual selection with another visual selection.
`V`, `gx`, ..., `.` | Exchange a linewise visual selection with the current line (same as `gxx`).
`V`, `gx`, ..., `V`, `.` | Exchange a linewise visual selection with selected lines.

[1] Optional. Support selection direction for charwise exchange.
Some ideas:
- Simply paste in the same direction the selection was made, similar to motions.
- Implement a keymap (`gX`) for selecting without direction awareness.
- Use `.` for pasting forward and `,` for pasting backward.
...

comment_data.body:
'mini.operators' already supports visual selection in a way that is reasonable for custom operators. Pressing `gx` on *already* visually selected region uses it for the current exchange step (either first for "remembering" or second for doing exchange).

What it doesn't support from what you are describing is dot-repeating the action which was previously done on visual selection. This is mostly for several reasons:
- Even for built-in operators, dot-repeating an action after the previous was done for visual selection is fairly limited: it repeats the action on the same size region but applied at cursor. For example: `vipd` on a 3 line paragraph followed by `.` in 10 line paragraph will not delete whole 10 paragraph lines but only 3 at cursor.
- Making dot-repeat possible even at current level of support for "exchange" as operator (`gxiw` once, and then `.`  will work for `iw` at cursor at any "exchange stage") is fairly convoluted. Making it even more complex would probably be not great in the long term.

There *was* the precedent, though, for 'mini.comment' in efa0eb3dc97398e0510372f61bcf625127ab7a24 to make `gc` be dot-repeatable like built-in operators even after initially done for visual selection. That even resulted into *less* code and complexity. Unfortunately, quick testing showed that this is not as straightforward with 'mini.operators'.

All in all, I don't think adding dot-repeatability for exchange operator after a visual selection is worth it. If anything, suggesting to more often use operators is not a bad idea.
